- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; cap forecast overshoot at +3% above immediate prior peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above true mean, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period corrections; add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative after peak.
